extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and attorneys appearing before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order in a USPTO disciplinary matter describing stipulated facts, legal conclusions (violations of USPTO professional conduct rules), sanctions (reprimand, probation, possible suspension), publication requirements, and procedural enforcement steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional authority for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes statutory and regulatory authority for initiating and resolving disciplinary proceedings against registered practitioners before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO professional conduct rules to registered practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered practitioners are subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.) and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's registration subjects them to these ethical rules even if they maintain other credentials; conduct is evaluated under these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on holding oneself out as an attorney while not an attorney (37 C.F.R. § 10.31(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation to hold oneself out as an attorney while not an attorney. Example facts: including a signature block stating 'Associate General Counsel' and executing a joint representation agreement referring to the person as 'attorney' while not authorized to practice law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting titles, signature blocks, or agreement language that imply attorney status when not authorized constitutes a violation. The Final Order cites these specific facts as violating § 10.31(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on practicing law while suspended or otherwise unauthorized
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is administratively suspended from a state bar (and therefore not licensed to practice particular law) must not provide legal opinions, settlement positions, or negotiate legal disputes on behalf of clients while not authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in the case: while administratively suspended from the Wisconsin bar, the respondent communicated with opposing counsel, presented legal opinions and settlement positions on behalf of clients — conduct deemed practicing law and prohibited while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to investigate whether actions constitute the practice of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are expected to make a diligent investigation as to whether their actions constitute the practice of law; failure to do so is a basis for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parties agreed the respondent did not make a diligent investigation and later admitted the actions constituted the practice of law — mistake of belief without investigation is not a defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public reprimand may be imposed as a disciplinary sanction and will be published per Office procedures (e.g., Official Gazette, FOIA reading room).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: probation for 36 months under 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a thirty-six (36) month probationary period commencing on the date of the Final Order and shall be placed on probation pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4) for three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation can include conditions and enables monitoring; noncompliance during probation can trigger further enforcement (see Order to Show Cause / suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement procedure: Order to Show Cause and potential immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director in good faith opines that the respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall: (i) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend the respondent for up to six months; (ii) send the Order to Show Cause to the respondent at the last address of record; and (iii) grant the respondent thirty (30) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after considering any response, the OED Director remains of the opinion that the respondent failed to comply, the OED Director will deliver the Order to Show Cause, the respondent's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to six months. The OED Director may also seek discipline for the underlying misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension not stayed by review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director suspends the respondent pursuant to the enforcement procedures and the respondent seeks review of the suspension, such review shall not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An administrative review of a suspension does not automatically stay the suspension; the suspension takes effect despite a pending review.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 (publication/notice requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.59 governs notice and publication obligations for disciplinary actions; the Final Order explicitly instructs OED to follow that regulation in publishing the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided notice of reprimand and probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the exact text of the Official Gazette notice and requires public dissemination of the reprimand and probation details (including the factual summary and admonition to comply with Rules of Professional Conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in addressing any further complaint of the same or similar misconduct or in any future disciplinary proceeding against the respondent, including using the record as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past disciplinary records may be invoked later to increase discipline or to counter claims made by or on behalf of the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement to move to dismiss related proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall file a motion with the administrative law judge requesting the dismissal of the pending disciplinary proceeding within fourteen (14) days of the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a timeline to conclude related administrative matters consistent with the settlement and Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement allocates costs equally (each party bears its own), indicating no fee-shifting in this matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: General admonition to comply with USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents are reminded of their obligation to comply with the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order functions also as a reminder and warning to other registered practitioners about compliance expectations.
